steps.text: Conduction is the transfer of heat through a material. Let's compare how well a metal and a non-metal carry heat.
Tap “Start” to heat both materials at once.
Watch the temperatures — the metal heats up quickly (good conductor), while the wood stays cool (poor conductor, an insulator).
Metals are good conductors of heat; non-metals like wood are insulators. That's why pans are metal but their handles are not.

coach.mission: Heat a metal and a non-metal and compare how fast each warms up.
whenStuck: Tap “Start” to run the heating experiment.
Compare the two temperatures as they rise.
whenWrong: The metal heats up fast (good conductor); the non-metal stays cool (insulator).
If it stayed cool, that material is a poor conductor of heat.
whenCorrect: Right — the metal conducted heat quickly.
Good — the non-metal stayed cool because it's an insulator.
coach.done: You've seen that metals conduct heat well and non-metals insulate. Run it again, or move on when you're ready.
